Eckhart Tolle: German-born spiritual teacher and author whose books present present-moment awareness in non-sectarian language.
Michael A. Singer: American author and meditation teacher who writes about observing thought and releasing emotional patterns.
Pema Chödrön: American Buddhist nun and teacher in the Shambhala tradition, associated with Gampo Abbey in Nova Scotia.
Gabor Maté: Hungarian-born Canadian physician and author who writes on stress, trauma and illness.
Raymond Buckland: English-born author who helped introduce Gardnerian Wicca to the United States and wrote widely on witchcraft and the occult.
Scott Cunningham: American author of popular guides to Wicca and magical practice. He died in 1993.
Judika Illes: American author of reference works on magic, spells and witchcraft traditions.
Rachel Pollack: American writer and tarot scholar whose Seventy-Eight Degrees of Wisdom became a standard text on the cards.
Mantak Chia: Thai-born Taoist teacher and founder of the Healing Tao system, which he has presented to Western students since the 1970s.
Michael Winn: American teacher of Taoist practice and co-author of several Healing Tao books.
Elaine Pagels: Religion professor at Princeton University and author of studies on Gnosticism and early Christianity.
Thomas Ashley-Farrand: American author and teacher of Sanskrit mantra practice.
J.K. Rowling: British author of the Harry Potter series.
J.R.R. Tolkien: English author and philologist, creator of Middle-earth.
Ursula K. Le Guin: American author of the Earthsea books and many other works of fantasy and science fiction. She died in 2018.
C.S. Lewis: Irish-born British writer and scholar, author of The Chronicles of Narnia.
Neil Gaiman: British author of novels, comics and short fiction.
Terry Pratchett: English author of the Discworld series. He died in 2015.
Susanna Clarke: English author of Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell.
Madeline Miller: American author of novels retelling Greek myth.
Patrick Rothfuss: American author of the Kingkiller Chronicle.
Brandon Sanderson: American fantasy author of the Mistborn and Stormlight Archive series.
George R.R. Martin: American author of A Song of Ice and Fire.
T.H. White: English author of The Once and Future King. He died in 1964.
British Library: The national library of the United Kingdom.
Shirley Jackson: American author of The Haunting of Hill House. She died in 1965.
Ray Bradbury: American author of fantasy, horror and science fiction.
Mikhail Bulgakov: Russian writer whose novel The Master and Margarita was published after his death.
Anne Rice: American author of the Vampire Chronicles. She died in 2021.
Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm: German scholars who collected and published folk and fairy tales in the early nineteenth century.
James George Frazer: Scottish social anthropologist (1854–1941), author of The Golden Bough.
Marcus Aurelius: Roman emperor from 161 to 180 and a Stoic writer.
Viktor E. Frankl: Austrian psychiatrist and founder of logotherapy.
